jobs.description: Black River Technical College is seeking qualified applicants for the position of Adult Education Instructor located primarily on the Paragould Campus. Teaching at other locations may sometimes be required of the instructor. This position may require evening or weekend hours. The job is a full-time, twelve-month position. The College is committed to a quality work environment and experience by providing the following benefits in addition to compensation: COLA and/or bonuses are provided whenever fiscally responsible Eight hours of sick leave monthly after fulfilling all work hours in a pay period Eight hours of vacation leave monthly after fulfilling all work hours in a pay period Vacation leave increases according to years of service schedule Eight hours per calendar year of education leave A portion of health insurance premium paid by BRTC $20,000 life insurance policy with premium paid by BRTC 14% minimum retirement contribution from BRTC each pay period 11 paid State Holidays per calendar year if employed full time during the date of those Holidays Tuition Waiver for Employee and dependents to BRTC DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: The Adult Education Instructor will teach Adult Basic Education, ESL, and GED courses. Subjects taught will include but not be limited to the GED test areas (literature, writing, social studies, science, and math) and adult basic education skill areas (language, math, and reading). The instructor may also be responsible for teaching ESL (English as a Second Language) classes, Distance and Virtual Learning, Integrated Education and Training, and workplace classes. In addition, the instructor will complete any professional development needed as determined by the Adult Education Division. Other responsibilities of the instructor include: administering the TABE assessment to determine individual skills and TABE post-tests to assess progress according to recommended guidelines, administering the GED Ready pre-test and making assignments or referrals based on the results, completing and maintaining appropriate student registration, attendance, and assessment records. SPECIAL SKILLS: Knowledge and experience using MS Word, Excel, Zoom, Go Meet (or another online meeting platform), and Canvas (or other open-source learning management platforms such as Moodle or Blackboard). The candidate must have the ability to be a self-starter and work remotely with students online. QUALIFICATIONS: The applicant must have a Bachelor's degree and possess a current Arkansas Teaching Certificate. In addition, Adult Education Certification is required within three years of the hire date. Applications will be taken until the position is filled. Interested candidates should submit a cover letter, resume, state application, and three references to: BLACK RIVER TECHNICAL COLLEGE Julie Edington, Executive Director of Human Resources P.O. Through supervising the Office of Student Life, the Dean of Students collaborates with a team of faculty & staff that provide a variety of student support services along with opportunities for leadership experience, engaging programming, and specialized resources.The Office of Student Life consists of several specialized programs, including Dining & Food Services, Disability Services, Emergency & Care Services, Facilities & Events Services, Housing & Campus Living, ID Card Office, Intramural & Recreation, New Student Programs, Parent & Family Programs, Student Activities, Student Leadership Programs, Student Conduct, Student Organizations, Testing Center, Vanguard Mascot, and Vanguard Volunteers. Emergency & Care Services The Dean of Students helps students and their families during difficult or emergency situations. Assistance includes outreach, advocacy, intervention, support and referrals to relevant campus and community resources. Please note our office does not provide counseling services. Learn More about Emergency Services Academic & Community Standards At the ASU-Beebe, we want students' continued education to be successful and engaging, and we care about the safety and well-being of our campus community. With this in mind, the ASU-Beebe has established clear academic & community standards through a document entitled the Student Code of Conduct, which communicates the collective expectations of members of the Vanguard community.The Dean of Students is responsible for the administration college's s academic & community standards and facilitation of the Student Conduct Process. Aiming to provide a safe and equitable campus community, potential violations of the Student Code of Conduct are investigated and adjudicated through a process designed to foster self-reflection, promote civility, and encourage personal responsibility. Acces Student Conduct Resources Student Leadership Programs The Dean of Students is proud to provide a variety of formats for students to participate in developing the leader within. Whether participating in student government, joining a student orgainzation, finding real-work leadership opportunities on campus, or attending one of our many workshops, there is room for everyone to develop leadership skills while attending ASU-Beebe. More About Leadership Opportunities Cocurricular Learning & Assessment It is the mission of the Office of Student Life to foster a campus environment that cultivates student learning through developing innovative co-curricular programming that enables students to become citizen leaders and engaged scholars within their community. Our educational priority is to enable residents to become citizen leaders and students as engaged scholars within their community. Students living on campus at ASU-Beebe will benefit from an environment that encourages learning through scholarship, citizenship, and leadership.Students at ASU-Beebe have the opportunity to participate in numerous experiences that promote learning. As the Office of Student Life assessed what experiences and outcomes students should gain while participating in campus life, four broad categories were identified which will serve as the center of campus life programming. Just like the arch which has historically stood in the center of the ASU-Beebe campus, we have labeled the outcomes ARCH, or:Academic & College SuccessRespect for Self & OthersCommunity & Leadership EngagementHealth & Personal WellnessAll campus life events and programming are designed to provide opportunities for students to engage with the ARCH Campus Life Curriculum's 16 cocurricular learning outcomes. The Dean of Students is responsible for assessing cocurricular learning for student life programming. Prohibition of Campus Hazing A learning community must be one where students can engage with peers, faculty, and staff in a safe environment, free of intimidation or threat of marginalization. As a result, and in compliance with state and federal laws, ASU-Beebe strictly prohibits hazing in any form. An individual’s participation in our learning community through registered student organizations, programs, or activities should be supportive and enhance, not undermine, the academic experience at ASU-Beebe. The initiation, admission, or membership of a registered student organization, program, or activity affiliated with the college should be one based on the community’s collective expectations of civility, respect, morality, and ethical behavior. Important Info Report an IncidentASU-Beebe is dedicated to providing a safe, secure learning environment for our campus community. You can help by reporting student concerns, student conduct violations, sexual misconduct or other potential threats to campus safety. This position is governed by state and federal laws and agency/institution policy. The University of Central Arkansas’s Department of Film, Theatre, and Creative Writing invites applications for a one-year, nine-month, Visiting Assistant Professor of Creative Writing (Fiction/YA Literature), beginning August 16, 2026. The successful candidate will have a terminal degree in Creative Writing or closely related field, publications in national literary magazines and/or peer-reviewed journals, experience teaching at the university level, and a commitment to supporting the university’s initiatives in serving a regional 4-year institution’s student body. This position requires teaching undergraduate and graduate courses, pursuing creative work, and programmatic service with a reliable campus presence.The position is non-tenure track. Job Duties and Responsibilities The UCA Creative Writing Program offers a BA in Creative Writing and an MFA in Creative Writing, supporting an undergraduate literary magazine, a graduate-run national literary magazine, an on-campus literary festival, and multiple nationally recognized visiting writers each year. The program is committed to supporting and enhancing an environment that values all perspectives and cultural backgrounds. Its mission is to develop creative writers, editors, and publishers through the combination of storytelling, community engagement, and critical thinking. The ideal candidate will: Support the creative writing program’s mission; Demonstrate excellent teaching skills at the university level with an innovative and responsive approach to the ever-changing and varied needs of our student body; Serve the program and participate in robust literary activities on campus; Create and maintain collegial, harmonious working relationships with an energetic faculty representing various perspectives; Show productivity in one’s artistic and scholarly life. The position carries a 4-4 annual course load. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities The successful candidate will teach fiction and writing for children and YA readers.
